result.title: STABLE: A Continual Learning Optimizer with Adaptive Drift Control
result.comment: Accepted at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
result.summary: Continual learning suffers from catastrophic forgetting, leading to the loss of past knowledge and unstable adaptation across task streams. Existing approaches typically address this issue through replay buffers, architectural changes, or additional regularization terms. We argue that forgetting is a consequence of unstable learning dynamics, which may benefit from an optimizer-level solution. The main challenge is that learning dynamics are time-dependent, as demonstrated by empirical phenomena such as the stability gap. First, we formally prove that, for distance-based classifiers, bounded parameter drift guarantees bounded margin erosion under a local score-stability condition. Based on this insight, we propose STABLE, a primal-dual optimizer with adaptive drift control. STABLE enforces a drift budget by increasing the dual variable when the budget is violated and decreasing it otherwise. This results in high stability without penalizing plasticity. Experiments on long-horizon unimodal streams and CLIP-based multimodal streams show that vanilla PEFT baselines trained with STABLE match or outperform specialized continual learning methods. In the multimodal setting, STABLE further preserves zero-shot transfer, matching or exceeding dedicated multimodal continual learning methods.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把灾难性遗忘归因于学习动力学不稳定，提出优化器层面的 STABLE：用原始-对偶方式自适应调节漂移预算（越界则增大对偶变量），并证明有界参数漂移可限制距离分类器的间隔侵蚀，在长序列单模态与 CLIP 多模态任务流上验证其可匹配或超过专用持续学习方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「漂移预算＋对偶调节」这一约束更新幅度、兼顾稳定性与可塑性的优化机制，可能可供核查用于抑制 VLM 适配或 latent 推理状态中视觉信息的漂移与坍缩；但论文作用于参数层而非推理期状态生成，迁移属推测。
